claims.quote: He pushed a small folder across his desk and said, as if reading from the edge of a map, "Holloway Gazette, mid‑March 1972 — photograph of Holloway House. Box 4, Folder 12. Accession HA‑1972‑03."
claims.value: Holloway Gazette, March 14, 1972, Box 4 Folder 12, accession HA-1972-03

claims.quote: The caption beneath the grainy photograph named the day: March 14, 1972.
claims.value: Hannah Hale, last seen in Holloway House, March 14, 1972.

claims.quote: The picture showed the mantel and the mirror in the same shape I'd learned by touch: the hairline seam across the silvering, the tall east windows throwing a wedge of light onto the floor.
claims.value: mantel, Venetian mirror with hairline seam, tall east windows

claims.quote: "Hannah fussed with her glass," she said. "She used to warn people about the seam — said you could feed a thing into it if you weren't careful. Mind the seam, love — and don't light it at noon."
claims.value: Mind the seam, love — and don't light it at noon.

claims.quote: One, headed March 9, 1972, said, "At the seam the glass receives what the room offers; mark the joint and do not let the light strike the wrong edge."
claims.value: At the seam the glass receives what the room offers; mark the joint and do not let the light strike the wrong edge.

claims.quote: Another, dated March 21, 1972, read, "Note the angle at the sill; when the light cuts the sill aright the seam answers and will not be denied."
claims.value: Note the angle at the sill; when the light cuts the sill aright the seam answers and will not be denied.

claims.quote: If the silvering included a seam that functioned like a channel, then a beam arriving at a particular declination could be the activating condition. That activation would obey optics, not omen: an aligned ray traveling to the seam, unbroken, might produce the reflection effects I had already noticed.
claims.value: Mirror activates under a precise light alignment hitting the seam in the silvering, consistent with reflection-conduction rules.

claims.quote: Prediction one: reproduce the March sun's angle with my oil lamp and the mirror will show the lagged echo again and an intensified shimmer at the seam. I set a tentative placement on the sketch — lamp six feet from the mantel, flame roughly eighteen inches above the hearth, and aligned seven inches left of the mirror's center mark.
claims.value: Place oil lamp six feet from the mantel, flame 18 inches above the hearth, aligned 7 inches left of mirror center to reproduce effect.

claims.quote: Prediction two: interrupting the reflective path by covering the seam with an opaque strip or placing a board across the sill will stop the lag and the shimmer, proving the effect needs an unobstructed reflective route.
claims.value: Covering the seam or interrupting the reflective path will prevent the mirror's lag/shimmer effects.

claims.quote: I measured the six feet with the cheap tape and made the mark seven inches left of centre in pencil on the envelope I kept with the diary. The protractor from my toolbox was ready; the oil lamp was already ordered online.
claims.value: Will measure and set lamp as noted: six feet from mantel, wick at 18 in., mark 7 in left of center; will use protractor and tape.

promises.promise: Reader is owed a follow-up where Lena conducts controlled optical tests with measurements and lamp placement to investigate the reflection lag.
promises.quote: I made the hypothesis explicit and wrote down two simple, falsifiable predictions.
